newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: NAB to create Australian BNZ unit.
newsitem.headline: NAB to create Australian BNZ unit.

text.p: National Australia Bank Ltd said on Monday it would establish a new division called Bank of New Zealand Australia (BNZA) to take over the Australian banking business of Bank of New Zealand to meet Reserve Bank guidelines.

Bank of New Zealand was expected to cease to exist and its existing Australian activities to be subsumed into the BNZA unit late in the first half of calendar 1997, NAB chief general manager Frank Cicutto said in a statement.
The move reflects Reserve Bank policy that banks operating in Australia should have only one banking authority. The BNZA structure has Reserve Bank approval.

Bank of New Zealand customers would become BNZA customers with the unit continuing to target residential mortgage and investment lending markets as well as distribution through third party mortgage introducers, NAB said.
NAB would take over Bank of New Zealand's back office operations which would result in cost savings, spokesman Haydn Park told Reuters.
Park declined to specify how much NAB would save in the move.
